subject: general
question: In May 2025, which advanced research facility was inaugurated by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) with the aim to further strengthen indigenous quantum capabilities for strategic and defence applications?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Quantum Technology Research Centre, Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **May 2025**, the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** reached a significant milestone by inaugurating the **Quantum Technology Research Centre** located in **Delhi**.
 
• The primary objective of this advanced research facility is to strengthen **indigenous quantum capabilities** specifically tailored for **strategic and defence applications**, ensuring **national security** in an evolving technological landscape.
 
• The centre is dedicated to developing cutting-edge technologies such as **Quantum Key Distribution (QKD)**, **Quantum Communication**, and **Quantum Sensing** to provide secure data transmission and advanced detection systems for the armed forces.
 
• This initiative aligns with the vision of **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) by reducing dependency on foreign technologies for sensitive **cryptographic** and **surveillance** equipment.
 
• The facility acts as a hub for scientists and researchers to collaborate on **quantum computing** algorithms that can solve complex logistical and strategic problems much faster than classical computers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation):**
 
 
• Established in **1958**, it is the R&D wing of the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India.
 
• Headquartered in **New Delhi**, it oversees a network of more than **50 laboratories** developing diverse technologies in **aeronautics**, **armaments**, **electronics**, and **missile systems**.
 
• The organization plays a pivotal role in maintaining the **technological edge** of the Indian Military through local innovation.
 
 
 
• **National Quantum Mission (NQM):**
 
 
• Approved by the Union Cabinet in **2023** with a total outlay of over **Rs. 6,000 crore**.
 
• The mission aims to seed, nurture, and scale up scientific and industrial R&D in **Quantum Technology (QT)** over the next **eight years**.
 
• It targets the development of **intermediate-scale quantum computers** with **50-1000 physical qubits** in various platforms.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of Quantum Tech:**
 
 
• **Quantum Key Distribution (QKD)**: Allows two parties to produce a shared random secret key known only to them, which can be used to encrypt and decrypt messages, making them immune to **hacking**.
 
• **Quantum Radar**: Utilizes quantum entanglement to detect **stealth aircraft** and objects that are otherwise invisible to conventional radar systems.
 
• **Precision Timing**: Quantum clocks provide highly accurate time synchronization, which is critical for **GPS** and **navigation systems** during wartime.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geospatial Advantage:** Establishing the centre in **Delhi** facilitates seamless coordination between **DRDO Headquarters**, the **Ministry of Defence**, and academic powerhouses like **IIT Delhi**.
 
• **Future Readiness:** The **May 2025** inauguration signifies India's commitment to staying ahead in the **global quantum race**, which is currently dominated by nations like the **USA** and **China**.
 
• **Indigenous Development:** Most of the hardware and software protocols developed at the **Quantum Technology Research Centre** are built from the ground up to prevent **backdoor vulnerabilities** in military hardware.
 
• **Dual-use Nature:** While the primary focus is **defence**, the breakthroughs achieved here in **quantum sensors** can also be applied to **civilian sectors** like healthcare and disaster management.
